mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, interpret both sides as signed equations preserving the order of names (e.g., (A - B) = (C - D)).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you encounter a sentence of the form 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have' or any equality of differences.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the number of peaches that A has more than B equals the difference between C and D' as |A - B| = |C - D| (absolute values) would be wrong.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and simplify, repeatedly propagating known values until no further simplifications are possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each direct count, transfer, or solved equation, update all other equations that involve the same variable.
mathgap.example: Leaving an equation like A - B = 5 unchanged after learning A = 10, instead of substituting to get B = 5, leads to missed deductions.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the text, after applying any earlier transfers or overrides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a 'has K more/fewer than' or similar comparative sentence, ensure all prior statements (including transfers) have been applied.
mathgap.example: Evaluating 'A has 3 more than B' before processing a prior transfer that gave B additional items would give the wrong relationship.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations that involve the queried person directly or indirectly, and solve only that subsystem to avoid unnecessary complexity.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving the whole system, trace connections from the query variable through equations to isolate relevant variables.
mathgap.example: Including unrelated equations about people who never appear in any chain leading to the query wastes effort and can cause confusion.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similarly spelled names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the text, map each distinct name token to its own variable.
mathgap.example: Merging 'Kaila' and 'Kaila' (typo) or treating 'James' and 'Jamess' as the same would cause incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says 'the difference between the number of X that A and B have', interpret it as the signed difference A - B, preserving the order of the names as given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any time you see 'difference between ... A and B' or similar, do not take absolute value; keep the sign.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between A and B' as |A - B| would lose sign information.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as A - B = K, and 'A has K fewer than B' as A - B = -K, preserving the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence contains 'more' or 'fewer' between two names.
mathgap.example: Swapping the sides and writing B - A = K would invert the relationship.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N items', set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears, replace the current value of that variable, even if it was previously derived from other equations.
mathgap.example: Treating a later 'X has 10' as an additional constraint rather than overriding the earlier value would cause inconsistency.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver, updating their counts before processing subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'X gives K items to Y' sentence appears.
mathgap.example: Treating transfers as simultaneous constraints without order would ignore the effect on later comparative statements.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often reverses the subtraction order, interpreting 'A has K more than B' as B - A = K instead of A - B = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'has K more than' defines a signed difference with the subject on the left: write A - B = K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when encountering 'difference between' or equality-of-differences, using |A - B| instead of A - B.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order of names and keep the signed difference; do not take absolute values.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats all transfers as simultaneous constraints, failing to update counts before later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer in the order it appears, updating giver and receiver counts before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are fixed initial values and does not override them when later statements provide a new count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, set the variable to that value at that point, overriding any previous value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model sometimes reads phrases like 'twice as many' as addition rather than multiplication.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Identify multiplicative language (e.g., 'twice', 'double') and translate it into multiplication, not addition.
